1389.title: Chairman Culberson Statement on the FY 2016 Commerce, Justice, and Science Appropriations Bill
1389.description:
On June 2, 2015, House Committee on Appropriations Subcommittee on Commerce, Justice, and Science Chairman John Culberson spoke on the House floor in support of H.R. 2578, the Fiscal Year 2016 Commerce, Justice, Science Appropriations Bill.'

On June 3, 2015, the U.S. House approved the fiscal year 2016 Commerce, Justice, Science Appropriations bill on a vote of 242-183. The bill funds the Department of Commerce, the Department of Justice, the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), the National Science Foundation (NSF), and other related agencies.

The legislation contains $51.4 billion in total discretionary funding, an increase of $1.3 billion over fiscal year 2015 and $661 million below the President’s request for these programs. The bill prioritizes funding for law enforcement, national security, science, and space exploration programs.

1400.title: Chairman Dent Floor Statement on FY16 Military Construction & Veterans Affairs Funding Bill
1400.description:
On April 29, 2015, House Appropriations Subcommittee on Military Construction and Veterans Affairs Chairman Charlie Dent spoke on the House floor in support of H.R. 2029, the FY 2016 Military Construction and Veterans Affairs Appropriations bill

To read his full statement, please visit: http://appropriations.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=394180

The legislation contains funding to house, train, and equip military personnel, provide housing and services to military families, and help maintain base infrastructure. The bill also funds veterans’ benefits and programs. In total, the bill provides $76.6 billion in discretionary funding – $4.6 billion above the fiscal year 2015 level. This represents a 5.6 percent increase over the fiscal year 2015 level for the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) – including increases for health care, benefit claims processing, the Board of Veterans Appeals, medical and prosthetic research, and information technology. Of this funding, $58.7 billion was provided in the fiscal year 2015 appropriations bill. Military construction is increased by $904 million over the fiscal year 2015 enacted level, which allows for full funding of family housing, construction of hospitals and health facilities, and support for critical overseas investments.

1560.description: The House Committee on Appropriations Subcommittee on Commerce, Justice, Science, and Related Agencies holds an oversight hearing on federal investments in neuroscience research with Dr. John P. Holdren, Director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, and Dr. John C. Wingfield, Assistant Director, Directorate of Biological Sciences, National Science Foundation.

1561.title: Hearing: The State of Efforts to Stop Human Trafficking Hearing (EventID=101774)
1561.description:
On February 26, 2014, the House Committee on Appropriations Subcommittee on Commerce, Justice, Science, and Related Agencies reviews the state of efforts to end human trafficking. Witnesses include Ms. Stephanie Vu, a human trafficking survivor-advocate; Detective William Woolf of the Fairfax County Police Department; Ms. Cindy McCain, Co-Chairperson of the Arizona Governor's Task Force on Human Trafficking; and Mr. John D. Ryan, President and CEO of the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children.

To view the full video of the hearing at its conclusion, as well as testimony and biographies from the witnesses, please visit: http://appropriations.house.gov/calendar/eventsingle.aspx?EventID=370030

1562.title: Rogers: FY14 Omnibus Prioritizes Important Programs, Cuts Federal Spending
1562.description:
House Committee on Appropriations Chairman Hal Rogers spoke on the floor of the United States House of Representatives to support the Fiscal Year 2014 Consolidated Appropriations legislation.

The bill funds every aspect of the federal government, from our national defense to our transportation systems, to the education of our kids. The bill reflects careful decisions to realign our nation's funding priorities and target precious tax dollars where they are needed most. For the fourth year in a row, federal discretionary spending is reduced - totaling $165 billion in cuts since Republicans took control of the House in 2011.

The bill passed the House by a vote of 359-67.

For the text of the statement, please visit: http://appropriations.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=366918

1563.title: Chairman Hal Rogers Lauds Ryan-Murray Budget Deal
1563.description:
House Appropriations Committee Chairman Hal Rogers spoke on the floor of the U.S. House of Representatives in support of the Bipartisan Budget Act of 2013, which provides topline discretionary spending levels for fiscal years 2014 and 2015.

The Ryan-Murray agreement will allow work to begin on legislation to fund the federal government for the remainder of the fiscal year, and avoid the potential for another government shutdown.

1564.title: Chairman Hal Rogers Commemorates the Late Congressman C.W. Bill Young
1564.description: House Committee on Appropriations Chairman Hal Rogers memorialized former Committee Chairman Bill Young in a special order speech on the jHouse floor on October 28, 2013. Chairman Young passed away on October 18, 2013. Chairman Rogers remembered him for his commitment to our troops and veterans, his leadership as an appropriator, and his dedication to the United States of America.

1565.title: Chairman Frelinghuysen Statement on the Nuclear Weapon Security and Non-Proliferation Act
1565.description:
On October 11, 2013, House Appropriations Energy and Water Subcommittee Chairman Rodney Frelinghuysen spoke on the House floor in support of H.J. Res. 76, the Nuclear Weapon Security and Non-Proliferation Act. The bill provides funding to maintain the United States' nuclear deterrent, secure vulnerable nuclear materials to keep them out of the hands of terrorists, and support the United States Navy's nuclear-powered submarines and aircraft carriers.

The House passed the bill on a vote of 248-176.

Read Chairman Frelinghuysen's statement here: http://appropriations.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=355329

http://appropriations.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=355329

1566.title: Chairman Rogers Statement on the Nuclear Weapon Security and Non-Proliferation Act
1566.description:
On October 11, 2013, House Appropriations Committee Chairman Hal Rogers spoke on the House floor in support of H.J. Res. 76, the Nuclear Weapon Security and Non-Proliferation Act. The bill would provide funding for the National Nuclear Security Administration to maintain our nuclear deterrents here at home, help ensure that nuclear weapons and materials don't fall into the wrong hands -- those of terrorists and other enemies to our nation. 

 The House approved the bill 248-176.

Read Chairman Rogers's full statement here: http://appropriations.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=355325

1567.title: Chairman Rogers Statement on H.J. Res. 90, the Flight Safety Act
1567.description:
House Appropriations Committee Chairman Hal Rogers gave the following statement on the House floor on October 9, 2013, in support of H.J. Res. 90, the Flight Safety Act. This bill would provide funding to resume operations within the Federal Aviation Administration that are critical to the safety of our skies and our aircraft fleet.

The House approved the bill on a vote of 252-172.

Read Chairman Rogers's full statement here: http://appropriations.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=353472

1568.title: Chairman Rogers Statement on H.J. Res. 91, the Honoring the Families of Fallen Soldiers Act
1568.description:
House Appropriations Committee Chairman Hal Rogers gave the following statement on the House floor on October 9, 2013, in support of H.J. Res. 91, the Honoring the Families of Fallen Soldiers Act. This bill ensures that funding is continued to guarantee that the government honors its commitments to military families, including providing a "death gratuity" to families of fallen soldiers - which helps assist them in their times of greatest need.

The House unanimously voted to approve the bill, 425-0.

Read Chairman Rogers's full statement here: http://appropriations.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=353471

1569.title: Chairman Rogers Statement on the Border Safety and Security Act
1569.description:
House Appropriations Committee Chairman Hal Rogers spoke on October 10, 2013, on the House floor in support of H.J. Res. 79, the Border Safety and Security Act. This bill would help protect our homeland from terrorists, drug traffickers, smugglers, and other criminals, and facilitate legal immigration and ongoing investigations.

The House approved this bill on a vote of 249-175.

Read Chairman Rogers's full statement here: http://appropriations.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=355236

1570.title: Chairman Rogers Statement on the Head Start for Low-Income Children Act
1570.description:
House Appropriations Committee Chairman Hal Rogers spoke on the House floor on Tuesday, October 8, in support of H.J. Res. 84, the Head Start for Low-Income Children Act. This bill would provide funding to keep Head Start programs open across the nation during the government shutdown. The House passed this bill on a vote of 248-168.

Read Chairman Rogers's full statement here: http://appropriations.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=353319

1571.title: Chairman Rogers Statement on the Food and Drug Safety Act
1571.description: House Appropriations Committee Chairman Hal Rogers gave the following statement before the House on Monday, October 7, in support of H.J. Res. 77, the Food and Drug Safety Act. The bill provides funding for critical food, drug, and medical device safety efforts at the FDA, and allow the FDA to spend and collect user fees. The House passed H.J. Res. 77 on a vote of 235-162.

1572.title: Chairman Rogers Statement on the Federal Employee Retroactive Pay Fairness Act
1572.description: House Appropriations Chairman Hal Rogers made the following statement on the House floor on Saturday, October 5, in support of H.R. 3223, the Federal Employee Retroactive Pay Fairness Act, which ensures that federal workers who have been furloughed during the government shutdown will receive back pay. The bill passed the House unanimously (407-0).

1573.title: Chairman Rogers Statement on the National Emergency and Disaster Recovery Act
1573.description:
House Appropriations Committee Chairman Hal Rogers spoke on the House floor on Friday, October 4, in support of H.J. Res. 85, the National Emergency and Disaster Recovery Act, which provides immediate, short-term funding for critical Federal Emergency Management Agency programs. The bill passed the House on a vote of 247-164.

Read Chairman Rogers's full statement here: http://appropriations.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=352430

1574.title: Chairman Rogers Floor Statement on the Nutrition Assistance for Low-Income Women and Children Act
1574.description:
House Appropriations Committee Chairman Hal Rogers spoke on the House floor on Friday, October 4, in support of H.J. Res. 75, the Nutrition Assistance for Low-Income Women and Children Act, which provides immediate funding for the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children program until December 15, 2013, or until another appropriations bill is enacted. 

8.7 million women, children and infants rely on this program for nutrition assistance.

The bill passed the House on a vote of 264-144.

Read Chairman Rogers's full statement here: http://appropriations.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=352456

1575.title: Chairman Hal Rogers Statement on the Honoring Our Promise to America's Veterans Act
1575.description:
On October 3, 2013, House Appropriations Committee Chairman Hal Rogers gave this statement on the House floor, in support of the Honoring Our Promise to America's Veterans Act, which passed the House on a vote of 258-157. This legislation continues funding for the processing and delivery of disability claims and other health benefits, at the current annual rate of approximately $82 billion, until December 15, or until we enact full-year appropriations.

Read his full statement here: http://appropriations.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=352297

1576.title: Chairman Rogers Statement on the Pay Our Guard and Reserve Act
1576.description:
House Appropriations Committee Chairman Hal Rogers gave the following statement on the Pay our Guard and Reserve Act, which passed on a vote of 265-160, on the House floor on October 3, 2013. The bill ensures that members of the National Guard and Reserve receive due compensation for their service throughout the government shutdown. 

Read the full statement here: http://appropriations.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=352279

1577.title: Chairman Hal Rogers Floor Statement on the Providing Local Funding for the District of Columbia Act
1577.description:
House Appropriations Committee Chairman Hal Rogers gave the following statement on the House floor on October 1, 2013, in support of the Providing Local Funding for the District of Columbia Act, which allows the District to utilize its local funding at an annual rate of $6.9 billion until December 15, 2013. 

Read his full statement here:http://appropriations.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=352027

1578.title: Chairman Hal Rogers Floor Statement on the Open Our Nation's Parks and Museums Act
1578.description:
House Appropriations Committee Chairman Hal Rogers gave this statement on the House floor on October 1, 2013, in support of the Open Our Nation's Parks and Museums Act, which provides funding for the National Park Service, Smithsonian Museums, and Holocaust Museum until December 15, 2013. 

Read his full statement here: http://appropriations.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=352025

1579.title: Chairman Hal Rogers Floor Statement on the Honoring Our Promise to America's Veterans Act
1579.description:
House Appropriations Committee Chairman Hal Rogers gave the following statement on the House floor on October 1, 2013, in support of the Honoring Our Promise to America's Veterans Act, which provides funding to process and delivery disability claims and services for our veterans until December 15, 2013. 

Read his full statement here: http://appropriations.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=352028

1580.title: Chairman Hal Rogers Supports Updated Bill Funding the Federal Government
1580.description:
House Committee on Appropriations Chairman Hal Rogers spoke on the House floor on September 28, 2013, in support of a House Amendment to the Senate's version continuing resolution H.J. Res. 59. This bill would have kept the federal government open for business after September 30, 2013.

Read his remarks here: http://appropriations.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=351679

1581.title: Chairman Hal Rogers Supports Move to
1581.description:
House Appropriations Committee Chairman Hal Rogers delivered a statement on the House floor on September 30, 2013, in support of the move by the House to go to conference committee on H.J. Res. 59, the Continuing Resolution to fund the government after midnight on September 30, 2013. A conference committee would allow time for the House and the Senate to come together, negotiate, and make an agreement on how best to fund the government. 

Read Chairman Rogers' full statement before the House of Representatives here: http://appropriations.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=351902

1582.title: Chairman Hal Rogers Presents H.J. Res. 59, a Bill to Prevent a Government Shutdown
1582.description: House Committee on Appropriations Chairman Hal Rogers presents H.J. Res. 59, the short-term continuing resolution to keep the government open after the end of the fiscal year on September 30, 2013. This bill provides funding at the current rate, prevents a government shutdown, and allows Congress to complete its important work addressing the nation's fiscal issues. The bill passed the House on September 20, 2013.

1583.title: Chairman Tom Latham Presents Bill Funding Transportation and Housing Programs for Fiscal Year 2014
1583.description: Subcommittee Chairman Tom Latham presents H.R. 2610, the Fiscal Year 2014 Transportation and Housing and Urban Development Appropriations Bill, on the House of Representatives floor on July 30, 2013. The bill provides $44.1 billion in funding for critical Department of Transportation programs, including FAA, federal highways, and safety programs, as well as housing programs for our most vulnerable citizens.

1584.title: Rep. Rodney Frelinghuysen Supports H.R. 2397, the FY14 Defense Appropriations Act
1584.description: Congressman Rodney Frelinghuysen spoke on the House of Representatives floor on July 23, 2013, in support of H.R. 2397, the Fiscal Year 2014 Department of Defense Appropriations Bill.

1585.title: Chairman Hal Rogers Asks the House of Representatives to Support Our Troops and National Security
1585.description:
House Appropriations Committee Chairman Hal Rogers of Kentucky spoke on the House of Representatives floor on July 23, 2013, in support of H.R. 2397, the Fiscal Year 2014 Department of Defense Appropriations Bill. 

Read his full statement here: http://appropriations.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=343611

1586.title: Chairman Bill Young Presents H.R. 2397, the FY 2014 Department of Defense Appropriations Bill
1586.description:
Defense Subcommittee Chairman Bill Young of Florida presents the Fiscal Year 2014 Department of Defense Appropriations Bill on the floor of the U.S. House of Representatives on July 23, 2013. The bill supports the United States' national security needs and ongoing military operations by providing funding for the Pentagon and the U.S. Armed Forces.

Read Chairman Young's full statement here: http://appropriations.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=343610

1587.title: Chairman Rodney Frelinghuysen Presents H.R. 2906, the FY14 Energy and Water Funding Bill
1587.description:
Subcommittee Chairman Rodney Frelinghuysen of New Jersey speaks before the U.S. House of Representatives to present the Fiscal Year 2014 Energy and Water Development Appropriations Bill on July 9, 2013. 

The House version of the legislation provides annual funding for national defense nuclear weapons activities, the Army Corps of Engineers, various programs under the Department of Energy, and other related agencies. For a summary of the bill, visit: http://appropriations.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=340615

1588.title: Chairman Hal Rogers Supports FY14 Military Construction and Veterans Appropriations Bill
1588.description:
On June 4, 2014, House Committee on Appropriations Chairman Hal Rogers spoke on the House of Representatives floor in support of H.R. 2216, the appropriations bill providing funding for military construction, veterans affairs, and related agencies for fiscal year 2014.

Chairman Rogers also expressed his hope that Congress will soon come to a budget compromise that eliminates sequestration, and gives a single, common, topline budget number for both the House and the Senate.

1589.title: Rep. John Culberson Presents FY14 Military Construction & Veterans Appropriations Bill
1589.description:
Chairman John Culberson speaks on the U.S. House floor on June 4, 2013, to present H.R. 2216, the bill funding military construction and veterans affairs programs for the 2014 fiscal year.

Chairman Culberson described the bill as "bipartisan," and noted that it addresses the "unacceptable" veterans disability claims backlog and need for an integrated Departments of Defense and Veterans Affairs electronic health record.

1590.title: Rep. Ander Crenshaw Discusses IRS Targeting Scandal on Fox News
1590.description:
Financial Services Subcommittee Chairman Ander Crenshaw appeared on "America Live" with Megyn Kelly on Fox News on June 3, 2013, to preview his Subcommittee's hearing with Acting IRS Commissioner Danny Werfel.

Chairman Crenshaw says the House Appropriations Committee wants answers about the IRS's practice of targeting conservative groups for added scrutiny, and wants to know what the Committee can do to ensure that this sort of inappropriate practice never happens again.

1591.title: House Appropriations Financial Services Subcommittee Reviews IRS Spending After News of Scandal
1591.description:
On June 3, 2013, the Financial Services Subcommittee of the House Committee on Appropriations met with Acting IRS Commissioner Danny Werfel and Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration J. Russell George to discuss the recent allegations that the IRS had inappropriately targeted conservative groups applying for tax-exempt status for additional scrutiny, as well as news that the IRS had spent $50 million on conferences over two years.

Subcommittee Chairman Ander Crenshaw here delivers his opening remarks, demanding answers from the IRS and formulating a plan to ensure the IRS never wastes or abuses tax dollars again.

1592.title: Chairman Hal Rogers Talks IRS Targeting and Spending on Fox News
1592.description: House Appropriations Committee Chairman Hal Rogers appeared on "America's Newsroom" on Fox News on June 3, 2013, to discuss the latest updates in the IRS story - including alleged wasteful spending on conferences and how Washington, DC, may have been involved in the targeting of conservative groups - and how the Committee will respond to this inappropriate behavior.

1593.title: Chairman Tom Latham Supports Bill to Help Reduce FAA Furloughs and Alleviate Flight Delays
1593.description: On April 26, 2013, House Committee on Appropriations Transportation Subcommittee Chairman Tom Latham of Iowa presented H.R. 1765, a bill that provides up to $253 million for FAA operations. This bill will help restore reliable and safe service in the American commercial air traffic system by reducing or eliminating employee furloughs that have caused delays recently.

1595.title: Appropriations Chairman Hal Rogers Supports Preventing Government Shutdown
1595.description: On March 21, 2013, House Committee on Appropriations Chairman Hal Rogers spoke on the U.S. House floor in support of H.R. 933, a bill that funds the federal government until September 30, 2013. This bill prevents a government shutdown, supports vital government programs and services, and maintains our national security.

1596.title: Chairman Hal Rogers Supports Bill to Prevent Government Shutdown, Support Our Troops and Veterans
1596.description: On March 6, 2013, House Appropriations Committee Chairman Hal Rogers urged the US House of Representatives to vote for H.R. 933. This bill provides funding to keep the government open, provide vital programs and services, and ensure a strong national defense. By avoiding a government shutdown, Congress can make the most of a bad situation and turn its attention to the serious fiscal challenges facing the nation.

1597.title: Chairman Rogers Urges Congress to Pass Emergency Funding for Hurricane Sandy Recovery
1597.description: House Committee on Appropriations Chairman Hal Rogers spoke on the U.S. House floor on January 15, 2013, in support of H.R. 152, a bill that provided emergency funding for Hurricane Sandy relief and recovery. President Obama signed the bill on January 29, 2013.

1598.title: Appropriations Chairman Hal Rogers on C-SPAN's Newsmakers
1598.description: House Committee on Appropriations Chairman Hal Rogers appeared on C-SPAN's Newsmakers program on September 16, 2012, to discuss the nation's current fiscal situation, what the Committee has done to help, and how we'll move forward.

1599.title: Chairman Rogers Supports Short-Term Funding Measure on House Floor
1599.description: On September 13, 2012, the House passed a short-term funding measure, also known as a Continuing Resolution, to keep the government operating at the start of the new fiscal year on October 1. Although not the preferred course of action, Chairman Rogers hailed the bill as a "good-faith effort to provide limited but fair funding for government programs." The bill also provides disaster relief and recovery funding.

1600.title: Defense Chairman Bill Young Presents FY13 Defense Spending Bill to House of Representatives
1600.description: On July 18, 2012, House Appropriations Defense Subcommittee Chairman C.W. Bill Young urged the House of Representatives to vote in favor of H.R. 5856, the Fiscal Year 2013 Defense Appropriations bill.

1601.title: House Appropriations Chairman Hal Rogers Supports Defense Spending Bill on House Floor
1601.description: On July 18, 2012, House Committee on Appropriations Chairman Hal Rogers urged the House of Representatives to vote in favor of H.R. 5856, the Fiscal Year 2013 Defense Appropriations bill.

1602.title: Chairman Rogers Supports FY13 Transportation, Housing and Urban Development Spending Bill
1602.description: House Committee on Appropriations Chairman Hal Rogers speaks on the U.S. House of Representatives floor in support of the FY13 Transportation, Housing and Urban Development spending bill on June 26, 2012.

1603.title: Chairman Tom Latham Supports FY13 Transportation, Housing and Urban Development Spending Bill
1603.description: House Committee on Appropriations Subcommittee on Transportation, Housing and Urban Development Tom Latham of Iowa speaks on the House floor in support of the FY13 THUD spending bill on June 26, 2012.

1604.title: Chairman Aderholt Introduces FY 2013 Homeland Security Appropriations Bill
1604.description: Subcommittee Chairman Robert Aderholt of Alabama introduced the Fiscal Year 2013 Homeland Security Appropriations bill on Wednesday, June 6, 2012, before the House of Representatives. This spending bill provides $39.1B for programs under the Department of Homeland Security, Coast Guard, TSA, ICE, CBP, and other integral agencies.

1605.title: Appropriations Chairman Hal Rogers Supports FY 2013 Homeland Security Appropriations Bill
1605.description: House Appropriations Chairman Hal Rogers of Kentucky spoke in support of the Fiscal Year 2013 Homeland Security Appropriations bill on the floor Wednesday, June 6, 2012. This spending bill provides $39.1B for programs under the Department of Homeland Security, Coast Guard, TSA, ICE, CBP, and other integral agencies.

1606.title: Chairman Frelinghuysen Introduces FY 2013 Energy and Water Appropriations Bill
1606.description: On May 31, 2012, Subcommittee Chairman Rodney Frelinghuysen of New Jersey introduced the Fiscal Year 2013 Energy and Water Development Appropriations bill on the House floor. The bill provides funding for the Department of Energy and related agencies.

1607.title: Chairman Rogers Supports FY 2013 Energy and Water Appropriations Bill
1607.description:
On May 31, 2012, House Appropriations Chairman Hal Rogers of Kentucky rose in support of H.R. 5325, the Fiscal Year 2013 Energy and Water Development Appropriations bill. 

The legislation provides the annual funding for the various agencies and programs under the Department of Energy (DoE) and other related agencies, and totals $32.1 billion -- a cut of $965 million below the President's budget request.

1608.title: Chairman Rogers Supports Military Construction and Veterans Affairs Spending Bill on House Floor
1608.description: House Appropriations Committee Chairman Hal Rogers of Kentucky spoke on May 31, 2012, to urge Congress to pass H.R. 5854, the Fiscal Year 2013 Military Construction and Veterans Affairs Appropriations Bill. The bill passed later that evening on a bipartisan vote of 407-12.

1609.title: Rep. John Culberson Presents Military Construction and Veterans Affairs Spending Bill to House
1609.description: Subcommittee Chairman John Culberson of Texas introduces the Fiscal Year 2013 Military Construction and Veterans Affairs Appropriations on the House floor on Thursday, May 31, 2012. The legislation, passed by the House that same day, totals $71.7 billion in discretionary funding for our warfighters and veterans.

1610.title: Hal Rogers Floor Statement on FY 2013 Commerce, Justice, Science Appropriations Bill
1610.description: House Appropriations Chairman Hal Rogers spoke in favor of the fiscal year 2013 Commerce, Justice, Science Appropriations Bill on the floor of the U.S. House of Representatives on May 8, 2012

1611.title: Chairman Frank Wolf Speaks on House Floor on FY 2013 Commerce, Justice, Science Appropriations Bill
1611.description: House Appropriations Subcommittee on Commerce, Justice, and Science Chairman Frank Wolf presented the fiscal year 2013 Commerce, Justice, Science Appropriations Bill on the floor of the U.S. House of Representatives on May 8, 2012

1612.title: Chairman Rogers on Continuing Resolution to Avoid Government Shutdown
1612.description: House Committee on Appropriations Chairman Hal Rogers spoke on September 21, 2011, on the House floor in support of a Continuing Resolution short-term spending bill that will keep the government operating and provide must-needed disaster recovery and relief funding.

1613.title: Chairman Rogers Speaks On FY 12 Interior and Environment Appropriations Bill
1613.description: On July 25, 2011, House Appropriations Chairman Hal Rogers spoke on the House floor in support of the Fiscal Year 2012 Interior, Environment and Related Appropriations Bill.

1614.title: Chairman Simpson Presents FY12 Interior and Environment Spending Bill
1614.description: House Appropriations Subcommittee on the Interior, Environment and Related Agencies Chairman Mike Simpson of Idaho address the House of Representatives in support of H.R. 2584, the Fiscal Year 2012 Interior and Environment Appropriations Bill, on July 25, 2011.

1615.title: Chairman Crenshaw Addresses House Floor on FY 2012 Legislative Branch Appropriations Bill
1615.description: On July 21, 2011, House Appropriations Subcommittee on the Legislative Branch Chairman Ander Crenshaw of Florida presented H.R. 2551, the Fiscal Year 2012 Legislative Branch Appropriations Bill.

1616.title: Chairman Rogers Supports FY12 Energy and Water Appropriations Bill
1616.description: House Committee on Appropriations Chairman Hal Rogers speaks on the House floor in support of H.R. 2354, the Fiscal Year 2012 Energy and Water Development Appropriations Bill on July 8, 2011.

1617.title: Chairwoman Granger Makes Opening Statement on Department of State FY12 Budget
1617.description: House Committee on Appropriations State, Foreign Operations and Related Agencies Chairwoman Kay Granger of Texas makes opening remarks at a hearing discussing the Department of State's fiscal year 2012 budget with Secretary Hillary Clinton on March 10, 2011.

1618.title: Chairman Rogers Supports FY12 Defense Appropriations Bill
1618.description: House Committee on Appropriations Chairman Hal Rogers of Kentucky speaks on the House floor in support of H.R. 2219, the Fiscal Year 2012 Defense Appropriations Bill, on June 23, 2011.

1619.title: Chairman Young on FY12 Defense Appropriations Bill
1619.description: House Committee on Appropriations Subcommittee on Defense Chairman C.W. Bill Young of Florida addresses the House floor in support of H.R. 2219, the Fiscal Year 2012 Defense Appropriations Bill, on June 23, 2011.

1620.title: Chairman Rogers Floor Statement on FY 2012 Agriculture Appropriations Bill
1620.description: House Committee on Appropriations Chairman Hal Rogers of Kentucky addresses the House of Representatives in support of H.R. 2112, the Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies Appropriations Bill for Fiscal Year 2012.

1621.title: Chairman Young Speaks on Defense Continuing Resolution
1621.description: Defense Appropriations Subcommittee Chairman CW Bill Young of Florida makes a statement on the necessity of funding for our military on the House floor on April 7, 2011.
